focus: historical snapshot copied to a temp root retains cold history across reload/restore

the real port commits byte-identical state before and after the change
a rejected commit installs nothing in either implementation

assertions.restoreAcceptsOlderSnapshots: lib/dockyard-domain/memory.js#restore() still reads snapshot?.memoryState ?? snapshot?.state ?? snapshot, clones the input and raises the schema to at least 4; a read-only probe over schema 1-4 x raw/memoryState/state accepted all 12 shapes with the input detached.
assertions.committedDocumentNotAliased: test/domain-storage/domain-storage-write-path-equivalence.test.js asserts JSON.stringify(captured[i].document) === captured[i].json after later writes ("the committed value is never aliased to the live partition"), which is the contract the removed structuredClone in stateStore.update had to keep.

pinHostAcceptance.note: both official hosts ran the documented 21-step acceptance against the committed pinned tarball, into paths outside the package allow-list so the committed evidence was untouched.

postPublishHostAcceptance.note: both official hosts re-ran the full 21-step acceptance against the bytes downloaded anonymously from the published release, in a fresh official runtime and a fresh DSH_HOME.

ciRebuildContent.note: the CI runner rebuild has different compressed bytes (npm 10.9.3 on linux-x64) and the pinned content digest, which is the property the pin promises.

codeQL.note: CodeQL analysed the tagged commit with read-only content permissions and reported zero results; the repository has no open code scanning alerts (js/polynomial-redos and js/insecure-randomness are both fixed).

officialDSHIntegration: official bundle/profile mechanism only: package.json#dsh.bundle.patch points at cordis.patch.yml, which inserts the bundle by id/name. No patches/ directory, no patch-package, no install hooks, and no official DSH source file is modified in the acceptance path.

withdrawnCandidate.change: deleting the observation store created in openDomainStorage() as "dead code"
withdrawnCandidate.whyWithdrawn: the store is not read afterwards, but load() is not inert: snapshot() reads memory.hasColdHistory, which coerces every coldArchives entry. Removing it silently accepted the first commit after a corrupt durable state.
withdrawnCandidate.pinnedBy: test/domain-storage/domain-storage-write-path-equivalence.test.js — "a durable aggregate whose cold archive entry cannot be coerced still fails loudly" (fails with outcome "opened" if the two lines are removed)

releasedRemovals: installPending(): the second schema.parse of the document being committed (the full validation before installing staged files is unchanged)
createMemory(): the redundant structuredClone of the aggregate passed to stateStore.update
EvolutionMemory#save(): the full snapshot() deep copy, avoided by declaring inlineSerialization: true on that store

adversarialReview.scope: independent review by a different model of the rc.9 write-path removals against the rc.8 pin
confirmed: only the three removals are present; lib/ diff rc.8 -> rc.9 touches only lib/domain-storage.js
the withdrawn observation-store change is absent and the regression test fails if it is reapplied
committed bytes are byte-identical across the change (differential test anchored to release/dsh-evolution-0.2.0-rc.8.tgz)
no place where an updater mutates its argument, no caller-visible object aliased into persisted state, and no path that installs staged files before the full validation

findings.severity: pre-existing, not introduced by rc.8 or rc.9
findings.detail: memory.hasColdHistory uses Object.values(coldArchives).some(...), which short-circuits: when a coldArchives entry with count > 0 precedes a non-coercible entry, the corrupt entry is not reached and the durable aggregate is accepted. Identical bytes at v0.2.0-rc.7 (published), rc.8 and rc.9; the getter dates from the initial commit.
findings.decision: recorded as a known boundary instead of fixed, because fixing it changes shipped content and would invalidate the pin and the acceptance already performed on these bytes

coverageGaps: no committed regression test pins the legacy Memory restore snapshot formats (schema 1-3, memoryState/state wrappers); they were verified by a read-only probe only
the byte-differential equivalence workload exercises observe(); signed-event replay and successful pending-install recovery are not byte-diffed between rc.8 and rc.9

releaseNotes.note: the generated notes were extended with the verification summary, the post-publish section and the known boundary. Asset ids, sizes, digests and updated_at were re-checked after the edit and are unchanged.

observations: v0.2.0-rc.8 was pinned locally but never tagged or published; its tarball is only reachable from git history (release/dsh-evolution-0.2.0-rc.8.tgz) and its lib/ sources are the baseline the rc.9 differential test anchors against.
release/SHA256SUMS pins only the current version; the rc.1-rc.7 checksum files live in their own releases and were not rewritten.
the CI host-acceptance job installs a linux rebuild of the same tree, so its recorded tarballSha256 is the linux byte hash while its contentSha256 equals the pin.
remainingRisksAndUnverified: memory.hasColdHistory short-circuits on the first hit, so a corrupt coldArchives entry after a count > 0 entry is not detected. Present since the initial commit and identical in v0.2.0-rc.7, rc.8 and rc.9; left unfixed to keep the published bytes equal to the accepted bytes.

the published bytes are the committed bytes under release/, not a CI rebuild (deliberate; npm compression varies by npm version). pack:check, release:verify and test/release-pin.test.mjs all fail on any drift between the two.

v0.2.0-rc.1 tag/Release bytes still disagree (the tag names 98a6425 / d24f5e52..., the release serves fc41f0e0...). Unchanged by this release; fixing it would require moving the tag or overwriting assets, both out of scope.
legacy Memory restore snapshot formats (schema 1-3, memoryState/state wrappers) are verified by a probe but not pinned by a committed regression test.
byte-differential equivalence covers the observe() workload, not signed-event replay or successful pending-install recovery.
the guard remains a heuristic policy check, not a shell/JavaScript sandbox; promotion executes host code under trusted approval.
the acceptance does not cover manually disposing the underlying bundle Fiber.
the domain evaluator stays advisory; continuous/ and governance/ are unit-tested but not wired into the live loop.
internal/undocumented host interfaces are still used (ctx.events._hooks, ctx.reflect._getImpl() fallback, loader EntryTree.resolve, Entry.fiber/options/disabled).
event-bridge.key has no rotation or revocation flow; it is created once per data root and survives disable and uninstall.
no npm publish, no code signing/provenance (SLSA) and no SBOM for this RC.
the file-backend failure memory is still last-writer-wins and save() does not fsync.
the 0.2.1-alpha.1 npm dist-tag can move; the acceptance is pinned to that exact version.
see RELEASE.md section 6 for the full list; the entries above are the ones re-checked or newly observed for rc.9.

finalState.note: the audit files live outside the package allow-list, so this commit cannot change the published bytes or the pin.
